simple.meaning: הֶאָח (heʼâch) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “aha!.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 12 times across Job, Psalms, Isaiah, Ezekiel, beginning at Job 39:25. Its contexts include land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הֶאָח (H1889).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: הֶאָח (heʼâch) / H1889 is traced through Job 39:25, Psalms 35:21, Psalms 35:25, Psalms 40:16 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H1889. heach הֶאָח interjection (onomatopoetic) expressing joy, Aha! always introduced by אָמַר , Isa 44:16 he says, Aha , I am warm, I have seen the fire. Of satisfaction over the misfortune of an enemy or rival, Psa 35:21 ; 35:25 let them not say in their heart נַפְשֵׁנוּ הֶאָח Aha , so would we have it ! ( lit our desire !) 40:16 (= 70:4 ), Ezek 25:3 ; 26:2 ; 36:2 . Metaph., of the neighing of a war horse in the battle, Job 39:25 .
